# End-to-end tune-loop verification + full suite

> **Headline:** Verify the `--tune` loop end-to-end on the real CSV data (child of AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715): run the worked example, re-run for byte-identical determinism, confirm clean-checkout restore on success and failure, and pass the full project test suite. Covers parent AC1/AC3/AC4/AC8.

## Goal

- **As a producer**, I want recorded evidence that the `--tune` loop works end-to-end: the three artifacts are produced, determinism holds byte-for-byte, the checkout is left clean on success and failure, and the full suite passes.

## Expected behaviour

- Run the documented worked example (e.g. `--tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=6 --games 100 --out <dir>`), capturing the three artifacts and the summary.
- Re-run the identical tune command to a second directory and diff the comparison artifact (empty diff expected); confirm a no-op/empty edit yields zero deltas.
- Verify the CSV is byte-identical and the working tree clean after the run; force a mid-run failure path and confirm restore still happens.
- Run the full project test suite and confirm all tests pass. Record commit hash and evidence in a comment on the parent item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented end-to-end tune run produces the three artifacts (baseline, candidate, versioned before/after comparison) with meaningful per-metric and per-key deltas (parent AC1).
- Re-running the identical tune command yields a byte-identical comparison artifact, and a no-op edit yields empty (zero) deltas; the checkout is clean after success and after a forced failure (parent AC3/AC4).
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (parent AC8).

## Key Files

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — the exercised `--tune` command
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the worked example this run records
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — the CSV edited (and restored) by the tune run

## Notes

- Runs the tune loop on the real balance CSVs (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv` etc.) through the shared loaders; the checkout must be clean afterwards (the edit is restored).
data.title: End-to-end tune-loop verification + full suite

# Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

## Goal

Run the committed pipeline over the gathered footage to produce and validate
the actual deliverables and manifests: the ~45–60 s promo, the > 2 min
showreel, and several short highlight clips — all 960×540 WebM with the game's
SFX — accompanied by the selection and coverage manifests, and verify the
attention-grabbing pace criteria (AC1–AC4 of the parent).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can share a compelling promo package that
opens with action and showcases weapons, pickups and enemies.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Deliverables produced.** `capture-output/` contains: the compiled
  promo WebM (~45–60 s), the showreel WebM (> 2 min), and several highlight
  clips — all at 960×540 with an audio track (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback).
- **AC2 — Manifests produced.** The selection manifest (source WebM, series,
  mapped timestamps, motivating intensities) and the coverage manifest
  (feature → clip + timestamp ranges) accompany the deliverables; all three
  feature categories (weapons, pickups, enemies; boss when available) are
  listed.
- **AC3 — Pace verified.** The promo opens with action (no dead air in the
  first ~5 s) and cuts on peaks; verification measures the sampled non-black
  frame ratio and the average recorded intensity, and confirms they are at or
  above the documented reference band. The **reference band is documented**
  as part of this item (with the calibration basis).
- **AC4 — Per-clip intensities reported.** The manifest prints the per-clip
  recorded intensities so the pace claim is auditable.
- **AC5 — Validated.** Each deliverable passes the pipeline's validation step
  (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

- **Covers parent AC1:** **AC1 — Deliverables at full game-native resolution.** The work produces, written under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree: (a) a single compiled promo WebM of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (>2 min), and (c) several short highlight clips — all WebM (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback) at the game's **full native 960×540 resolution** (the game renders natively at 960×540: `src/core/constants.ts`), each carrying the game's own SFX audio track.

## Key files

- `capture-output/` — gitignored deliverables + manifests
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — the pipeline under test at runtime
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — reference band documented here

## Implementation notes

- This is a run/verify item: the *code* is delivered by the earlier items; this
  item executes the pipeline and records the evidence (file paths, durations,
  resolution, audio verdict, non-black ratio, mean intensity).
- If footage cannot evidence a category or the pace band is not met, record the
  gap explicitly and create a follow-up item rather than weakening the ACs.

## Deliverables

- The promo, showreel and highlight clips + both manifests + a pace report
  (comment on this item).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the ffmpeg driver (C5) and the gathered footage (C6).
data.title: Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

data.description:
## Goal

As a player, when I change the control scheme in Settings and then continue playing, the chosen scheme must be used by the ship — not only from the next run. Today, a scheme change made from the in-game Settings (pause menu) is persisted but the live ship keeps the old scheme for the rest of the run, so the chosen scheme is 'present but not honoured in gameplay'.

## Investigation (evidence)

Reproduced in a real headless Chromium against the current dev source (build -> boot -> play):

- Saving ai_hell_settings.controlScheme = 'fourDirectional' before starting a game -> PlayScene spawns the ship with fourDirectional (holding A translates, no rotation). **Works.**
- Saving 'asteroids' -> spawns asteroids (holding A rotates, no translation). **Works.**
- Full UI flow: Menu -> Settings -> cycle Control Scheme row -> Back -> Play -> the ship uses the new scheme. **Works.**
- Pause-menu flow: Play -> Esc -> Settings -> change scheme -> quit to menu -> Play -> ship uses the new scheme. **Works.**
- **Pause-menu mid-run flow: Play -> Esc -> Settings -> change scheme -> Back -> Resume -> the live ship keeps the OLD scheme for the rest of the run** (verified: scheme at start 'asteroids', stored becomes 'fourDirectional', live scheme after resume is still 'asteroids'). **Defect.**

Root cause: PlayScene resolves and applies the scheme once at ship spawn in create() (commit d45df97c, AC4 of AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA). On RESUME (returning from the pause menu) only _applyBindings() re-applies key bindings; the control scheme is deliberately not re-applied mid-run (intake decision Q2(a): 'applies on the next run / next ship spawn, never mid-run'). The operator's expectation ('When playing a game the chosen control scheme should be used') requires the chosen scheme to be honoured while the game is being played.

## Proposed implementation

- On PlayScene RESUME (or when the pause menu closes back into the run), resolve the effective scheme with resolvePlayerControlScheme(loadStoredControlScheme(), loadShipConfig()) and apply it to the live ship when it differs (Player.setScheme already swaps the movement model and input shape live; input dispatch reads player.getScheme() via the shared mapControlInput seam, so gym game parity is preserved).
- Keep spawn-time application as-is; a changed scheme therefore takes effect immediately on returning to the running game AND on the next run.
- Update the AC4 scene test that currently asserts 'does not swap the current ship when the setting changes mid-run' to the new expected behaviour; update docs (GDD §2.2, README) and the parent work item's AC4 note.
- Note: this reverses the recorded intake decision Q2(a) ('never mid-run') — needs operator confirmation before implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Changing the Control Scheme in the in-game Settings and resuming applies the chosen scheme to the live ship immediately (movement model + input mapping switch; verified by a scene test: saved fourDirectional then set mid-run -> the live ship drives four-directionally without a new run).
- AC2: Spawn-time behaviour is unchanged: a setting saved before a run still drives the ship from the first frame; resolution precedence (player setting -> ship config -> built-in default) unchanged.
- AC3: Bindings (rebindable keys) are unaffected; the shared mapControlInput seam is the only scheme->input mapping (gym game parity guards still pass).
- AC4: Settings row/save/restore behaviour unchanged; no CSV/config mutation.
- AC5: Full project test suite passes.

## Key files (predicted)

- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts — apply the resolved scheme on RESUME (and any other in-run settings-return path).
- src/scenes/PlayScene.controlScheme.test.ts — replace the mid-run no-change assertion with the new mid-run application assertion (additive: cover both 'applies on resume' and 'also applies on next run').
- docs/Game Design Document.md, README.md — note that a scheme change applies to the running game on resume (replaces 'next run only').
- Parent AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA AC4 wording/decision note to be updated (additive clarification).
data.title: Control scheme setting is not honoured during gameplay (mid-run)
